features.title: Keep the work moving, with its sources intact.
features.intro: Novels, scripts and videos keep their own content and revisions. Connect them when needed. When a source changes, inspect the affected scenes and shots before deciding what to remake.

items.title: Story facts and resources, clearly owned
items.body: Authors maintain characters, places and world rules. Research, designs and reference files retain their own sources and usage records.

items.title: A workspace for drama projects
items.body: Develop an original script from character and conflict, or compare an adaptation with its source. Continue through storyboards, previews and actual video while preserving versions and feedback.

items.title: Trace decisions from candidate to final
items.body: Compare reference drafts and asset candidates, request revisions or adopt them explicitly. Manuscript adoption and finalization stay separate, with history preserved.

workflow.title: Your Agent moves the work forward. You shape the story.
workflow.intro: Start with an idea, a draft or existing footage. Give your familiar Agent a goal, return to read or watch the result, then point to what needs changing and continue the same task.

steps.title: Give your Agent the goal and material
steps.body: Write a chapter, develop an episode or continue existing footage. Let your Agent prepare the work without retyping your conversation into forms.

steps.title: Read the result and choose what fits
steps.body: Read complete chapters or follow a script’s action and dialogue. Compare drafts and sources, give feedback and edit directly whenever you choose.

steps.title: Preview, then inspect real picture and sound
steps.body: Use an animatic for pacing and a simple 3D preview when staging needs it. Review representative generation before continuing to clips and an actual edit.

steps.title: Confirm a version and deliver usable work
steps.body: Script finalization, preview approval and final-cut confirmation are separate. Deliver the selected text, media and editable project with verified dependencies.

details.title: Suggestions are not canon
details.body: Discovered names, places and relationships remain candidates. Only author-confirmed content enters the story bible.

details.title: Checks are not literary judges
details.body: Rules inspect explicit facts and structure, reporting coverage and uncertainty. Motivation and literary choices stay with the author.

details.title: Review, adoption and finalization are separate
details.body: Review approval does not overwrite text. Adoption saves a new working revision; finalization records an author decision on an exact revision. Later edits retain earlier finals.

details.title: Deliver what the recipient can continue
details.body: Choose the exact text, video, audio, subtitles and project dependencies. Open the files in an independent reader or player, and verify the editing project separately.

open.title: Your next creative collaboration starts here.
open.body: Start with a novel, script or video. Keep the results, sources and choices in your own folders. Hetu is free and open source; external agents and generation services have their own accounts, pricing and terms.

integrations.eyebrow: Help your assistant understand your story
integrations.title: MCP, CLI and Skills. Direct access to your work.
integrations.intro: Let Codex, Claude Code or your preferred Agent organize a novel, develop a script or use your chosen tools to make previews, video and sound. Return to Hetu to read, watch, compare and give feedback.

layers.title: Give your Agent the goal
layers.body: From a new story idea to an existing manuscript, your Agent prepares the necessary details and operations. You do not have to retype the conversation into project forms.

layers.title: Continue with the work you already have
layers.body: Read scoped references, prepare inputs and drafts, and retrieve the actual result. Chapters, scripts, assets and handoffs share project records, so an interrupted task can resume.

layers.title: Review the result and make your choice
layers.body: Compare manuscripts and candidates, inspect proposed changes and give feedback. Adopt selected passages, finalize separately, and edit directly whenever you choose.

integrations.manual: A complete workflow without an agent
integrations.manualBody: Create books, write chapters and organize characters and world details yourself. Bring in an assistant when you want help and keep your own pace.

formats.title: Editable for authors. Readable for recipients.
formats.body: Deliver chapters and story facts for a novel, episodes and references for a script, or a finished video with subtitles, audio and an editable project. Fix the versions, choose the sources and assets to include, then verify that recipients can open, play and continue the work.

faq.title: Know the boundaries before you begin.

items.q: Do I need a novel to begin?
items.a: Start with a novel, an original script or a video. A script needs no placeholder novel; video can start from a brief, storyboards or existing clips. Link an authorized source revision when adapting, while each work keeps its own content, revisions and access scope.

items.q: Why not build another AI Agent inside Hetu Luoshu?
items.a: General agents require sustained work on reasoning, context, tools and execution recovery. We work with mature external agents and focus on creative content, story facts, resources, permissions and versions, with first-class MCP, CLI and Skills entry points.

items.q: Can an agent change my story bible?
items.a: An assistant working through a Hetu Luoshu task cannot unlock your story bible or approve final text for you. When using other tools, also check which files you have allowed them to access.

items.q: Will consistency checks detect every out-of-character moment?
items.a: No. Written facts about characters, time and world rules are easier to check; complex motivations and personality still need your judgment. Checks provide clues for your own review.

items.q: Which platforms and languages are included?
items.a: The current focus is Mac, with Simplified Chinese and English interfaces. Windows and mobile clients are not part of this release.

Download a Developer ID signed and Apple notarized Mac DMG or ZIP from GitHub Releases for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer. You can also try the homepage workspace or build from source using the developer guide.

items.q: Will my work be uploaded or become open source?
items.a: Your own books stay in the local folder you choose. Open-source software does not make your novel open source. You choose whether to share material with an external assistant or sync it elsewhere.

items.q: Can the work continue to a finished video and editable project?
items.a: Your external Agent uses selected tools for storyboards, previews, clips, sound and editing. Hetu retains the results for review. Preview approval and final-cut confirmation are separate; delivery includes checking subtitles, audio, assets and editable dependencies. Publishing and promotion are separate activities.

items.q: What are the license and costs?
items.a: Hetu is free and open source under Apache-2.0. Your work retains its own rights. External agents and generation services have their own accounts, pricing and terms. Optional Hetu model services use Lime Cloud accounts and credits; generation requires your approved content and spending scope.
